svg.title: The same system, fed two ways
svg.desc: Two panels. Graphiti: in the first run each session was cut into episodes of up to 8,000 characters, many messages in one episode; it answered 18% of the questions, the update was never stored in 45 of 67, at $0.24 per question. Fed one message per episode, as its own examples do, it answered 82%, the update was never stored in 5, at $0.64. Letta: in the first run each session was sent in one request ending on an assistant message, and the agent mostly took no step; 58%, 22 updates never stored, $0.03. With one agent step per user message it edited its memory about nine times per history; 69%, 15, $0.13.
svg.text: The same system, fed two ways
The first runs of two systems scored far lower than the others. Neither reported an error. Feeding them the conversation
the way each was built for changed the result; no setting was changed.
what one call to the system receives
First run: each session cut into episodes of up to 8,000
Each extraction prompt carried 60,000–80,000 characters, mostly
the assistant's answers. The model returned two or three entities
Second run: one episode per message, as Graphiti's own
The same revision now became a fact: “The user has completed
their 5th project since they began attending painting classes”.
First run: a whole session in one request, ending on an assistant
With nothing to reply to, the agent mostly took no step. Its block
about the user was empty after 43 of 67 histories.
Second run: one agent step per user message
The agent replied to each user message itself (the recorded
replies were not sent) and edited its memory about nine times per
